name: Overclaim
what: asserts more than anyone could know
affordance: asserts more than anyone could know — certainty as a costume
mechanism: drops qualifiers and states certainty past the evidence; the LLM-era twist: confident factual barrage is the most persuasive and least accurate register (Science 2025)
benign_reading: Strong claims are honest when the evidence really is strong; conviction is not a tell by itself. The tell is universal quantifiers and guarantees where no one could have the evidence.
ledger_line: {n} overclaim{s} — certainty stated past the evidence
output_phrasing: certainty is stated here past what the evidence could support

specimens.quote: I want you to listen to me. I'm going to say this again. I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky. I never told anybody to lie, not a single time—never.
specimens.speaker: President Bill Clinton
specimens.note: The absolute 'never... not a single time—never' universalizes a denial he later admitted was misleading; the quantifier wears certainty the evidence could not support.

specimens.quote: Let me start by telling you this: I have never used steroids, period. I do not know how to say it any more clearly than that. Never.
specimens.speaker: Rafael Palmeiro, Baltimore Orioles first baseman, sworn testimony to the House Committee on Government Reform
specimens.note: The doubled, freestanding 'Never.' stakes total certainty under oath as a substitute for evidence; he tested positive for the steroid stanozolol about four months later.

specimens.quote: Now, I have to tell you, it's an unbelievably complex subject. Nobody knew that healthcare could be so complicated.
specimens.speaker: President Donald Trump, remarks at a meeting with the National Governors Association
specimens.note: 'Nobody knew' projects the speaker's own surprise onto everyone, converting a personal knowledge gap into a universal excuse for a stalled repeal effort.

specimens.quote: Senator, yes. There will always be a version of Facebook that is free. It is our mission to try to help connect everyone around the world and to bring the world closer together.
specimens.speaker: Mark Zuckerberg, Facebook CEO, testimony (not under oath) before a joint hearing of the Senate Judiciary and Commerce Committees, answering Sen. Orrin Hatch
specimens.note: An unfalsifiable forever-guarantee ('always... free') plus mission-scale 'everyone' deflects the pay-for-privacy question at the Cambridge Analytica hearing; no one can know a company's pricing forever.

citations: Hackenburg et al. (2025). The levers of political persuasion with conversational AI. Science.

honest_twins.text: I checked every single row in the export — all 1,240 of them have a timestamp.
honest_twins.note: 'Every single' is honest here because the speaker actually performed an exhaustive check of a small finite set; the universal quantifier reports completed verification the listener can redo, rather than certainty worn as a costume.

honest_twins.text: I promise I'll have the draft to you by Friday morning.
honest_twins.note: 'I promise' is honest as a first-person commitment: it binds the speaker's own future conduct, which they control and are accountable for, instead of asserting a fact about the world that no one could know with that certainty.
